category: Fuel Cells, Electrolyzers, Electrolyte Transport & Electroanalysis
description: Hydrogen Fuel Cell (fc) and Water Electrolyzer (we) interfaces of the Fuel Cell & Electrolyzer Module with their phase, layer, reaction, gas-transport and water-management nodes, plus the Aqueous and Concentrated Electrolyte Transport, Electrode Shell and Electroanalysis interfaces of the electrochemistry modules. Java type strings come from COMSOL 6.4 Application Library models.

tools.name: Hydrogen Fuel Cell, Proton Exchange Membrane (fc)
tools.description: Model Wizard entry adding the Hydrogen Fuel Cell interface configured for PEM fuel cells: proton as charge-carrying ion, fuel-cell operation mode, humidified H2 and O2/air gas mixtures with gas-phase diffusion. The interface combines electrolyte (membrane/ionomer) and electronic charge transport, gas diffusion electrode kinetics, Maxwell-Stefan gas transport and optional Darcy flow in GDLs and channels, membrane water transport and gas crossover. Used for polarization curves, flow-field design, water management and thermal studies.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Electrochemistry > Hydrogen Fuel Cells > Proton Exchange Membrane (fc); Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("fc", "HydrogenFuelCell", "geom1")

parameters.name: prop("DefaultElectrodeReactionSettings") ChargeCarryingIon / OperationMode / TRHE
parameters.description: Proton, FuelCell, reference hydrogen electrode temperature.

parameters.name: prop("H2GasMixture"/"O2GasMixture") H2O, N2, GasPhaseDiffusion, GasMixtureDarcy
parameters.description: Species in each gas mixture and transport options.

parameters.name: prop("MembraneTransport") H2O_mem, H2_mem
parameters.description: Electroosmotic water drag and hydrogen crossover.

tools.notes: The fc and we interfaces are functionally identical; only defaults, names and icons differ. High-temperature PEM models (ht_pem) use the same interface.

tools.name: Hydrogen Fuel Cell, Solid Oxide (fc)
tools.description: Model Wizard entry of the Hydrogen Fuel Cell interface for solid oxide fuel cells: oxide ions as charge carrier, high reference temperature (default 700 degC) and H2/H2O fuel with N2/O2 air. Built-in equilibrium and thermoneutral potentials follow from species thermodynamics, and CO, CO2 and CH4 can be added to the fuel with the Water Gas Shift Reaction for reformate operation.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Electrochemistry > Hydrogen Fuel Cells > Solid Oxide (fc); Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("fc", "HydrogenFuelCell", "geom1"); prop("DefaultElectrodeReactionSettings").set("ChargeCarryingIon", "Oxide")
tools.notes: Couple Heat Transfer through Electrochemical Heating for thermal stresses and temperature gradients in stacks.

tools.name: Hydrogen Fuel Cell, Generic (fc) and Charge-Carrying Ion Settings
tools.description: The Generic entry and the Electrode Reaction Settings section of the fc/we interfaces choose the charge-carrying ion: Proton, Hydroxide (alkaline/anion-exchange cells), Carbonate (molten carbonate cells), Oxide (solid oxide) or Generic. The choice sets default reaction stoichiometry and the built-in reference hydrogen electrode used for equilibrium and thermoneutral potentials; with Generic, the RHE potential and ion charge are user-specified. The Operation mode (Fuel cell or Electrolyzer) sets default kinetics and stoichiometric-feed inlets.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Electrochemistry > Hydrogen Fuel Cells > Generic (fc); fc/we interface > Electrode Reaction Settings; Java: prop("DefaultElectrodeReactionSettings").set("ChargeCarryingIon", "Hydroxide")

parameters.name: ChargeCarryingIon
parameters.description: Proton, Hydroxide, Carbonate, Oxide or Generic.

parameters.name: Eeq_RHE, zion, Mion, Hion, Sion
parameters.description: Reference electrode potential and ion properties (Generic).

parameters.name: Phase
parameters.description: Solid or Liquid electrolyte phase of the ion.

tools.example:
Application Library: Fuel_Cell_and_Electrolyzer_Module/Fuel_Cells/ac_fuel_cell (Generic charge carrier, AC impedance of a fuel cell).
model.component("comp1").physics("fc").prop("DefaultElectrodeReactionSettings").set("ChargeCarryingIon", "Generic");
tools.notes: Ion entropy affects thermoneutral potentials but not equilibrium potentials versus RHE.

tools.name: Water Electrolyzer, Proton Exchange Membrane (we)
tools.description: Model Wizard entry adding the Water Electrolyzer interface configured for PEM water electrolysis: proton charge carrier, electrolyzer operation mode, liquid water in the reaction stoichiometry and humidified gas phases. The same layer nodes as the fuel-cell interface (membrane, porous transport/gas diffusion layers, catalyst layers as thin or porous GDEs) define the cell; outputs include polarization curves, overpotential breakdown and membrane hydration.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Electrochemistry > Water Electrolyzers > Proton Exchange Membrane (we); Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("we", "WaterElectrolyzer", "geom1")
tools.notes: For two-phase flow in porous transport layers combine with Phase Transport / Mixture Model interfaces (see pem_electrolyzer).

tools.name: Water Electrolyzer, Alkaline (we)
tools.description: Model Wizard entry for alkaline water electrolysis with hydroxide as the charge-carrying ion and a liquid electrolyte phase. Cells are built from H2/O2 Gas-Electrolyte Compartments (electrolyte plus evolved gas), a Separator (diaphragm), and H2/O2 Electrode Surfaces or gas diffusion electrodes; gas volume fraction reduces the effective electrolyte conductivity. Shunt currents in stacks and zero-gap designs are also modelled.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Electrochemistry > Water Electrolyzers > Alkaline (we); Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("we", "WaterElectrolyzer", "geom1"); prop("DefaultElectrodeReactionSettings").set("ChargeCarryingIon", "Hydroxide")

parameters.name: H2/O2 Gas-Electrolyte Compartment
parameters.description: Electrolyte and gas volume fractions, Bruggeman corrections.

tools.notes: Bubbly flow of the evolved gases can be solved with Euler-Euler or Mixture Model interfaces (alkaline_electrolyzer uses Euler-Euler).

tools.name: Water Electrolyzer, Solid Oxide (we)
tools.description: Model Wizard entry for solid oxide electrolysis cells (SOEC) with oxide-ion conduction, electrolyzer operation and high reference temperature. Steam (and CO2 for co-electrolysis) is fed to the hydrogen electrode; gas channels, gas diffusion electrodes and membrane define the cell, and the Water Gas Shift Reaction can be added for co-electrolysis.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Electrochemistry > Water Electrolyzers > Solid Oxide (we); Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("we", "WaterElectrolyzer", "geom1"); prop("DefaultElectrodeReactionSettings").set("ChargeCarryingIon", "Oxide")

parameters.name: H2 Gas Mixture: H2O, CO, CO2
H2/O2 Gas Flow Channel, Gas Diffusion Electrode

tools.notes: soec_thermodynamics shows an alternative setup with Secondary Current Distribution, Chemistry and Transport of Concentrated Species in porous media.

tools.name: H2/O2 Gas Mixture and Membrane Transport Settings (fc/we)
tools.description: Interface-level sections of the fuel cell and electrolyzer interfaces. H2 Gas Mixture and O2 Gas Mixture select the species present on each side (H2O, N2, CO2, CO, CH4 on the H2 side, auxiliary species), whether gas-phase diffusion (Maxwell-Stefan) and Darcy's law are solved, and whether liquid water appears in reaction stoichiometry. Electrolyte and Membrane Transport controls solving for the electrolyte potential, crossover species (H2, O2, N2) and electroosmotic water drag.
tools.usage: Hydrogen Fuel Cell / Water Electrolyzer > H2 Gas Mixture, O2 Gas Mixture, Electrolyte and Membrane Transport; Java: model.component("comp1").physics("fc").prop("H2GasMixture").set("GasPhaseDiffusion", "1")

parameters.name: H2O, N2, CO2, CO, CH4, aux
parameters.description: Include species in the gas mixture.

parameters.name: GasPhaseDiffusion
parameters.description: Include gas phase diffusion (needs more than one species).

parameters.name: GasMixtureDarcy
parameters.description: Use Darcy's law for momentum transport.

parameters.name: H2O_l
parameters.description: Use liquid water in reaction stoichiometry.

tools.notes: Instead of the built-in Darcy's law, a separate fluid flow interface can be coupled via Reacting Flow, H2/O2 Gas Phase.

tools.name: Electrolyte Phase / Electronic Conducting Phase (fc/we)
tools.description: Default phase nodes of the fuel cell and electrolyzer interfaces with locked selections. Electrolyte Phase solves the ionic charge balance (electrolyte conductivity) wherever Membrane, Separator, Gas Diffusion Electrode or Gas-Electrolyte Compartment nodes are active, or accepts a user-defined potential; Electronic Conducting Phase solves the electronic potential in Current Collector, GDE and GDL domains. Boundary conditions such as Electric Ground, Electric Potential and Electrode Current are added as their subnodes.
tools.usage: Hydrogen Fuel Cell > Electrolyte Phase (icph1) / Electronic Conducting Phase (ecph1) > Electric Ground, Electric Potential, Electrode Current; Java types: "ElectrolytePhase", "ElectronicConductingPhase"
tools.notes: Selections are defined by the layer nodes (Membrane, GDE, GDL...), not on the phase nodes themselves.

tools.name: H2 Gas Phase / O2 Gas Phase (fc/we)
tools.description: Default gas phase nodes defining gas transport in GDEs, GDLs, gas-electrolyte compartments and flow channels on each side of the cell. They set temperature/pressure inputs, gas diffusivities and, when diffusion is not solved, the composition as mole fractions, humidified mixture or humidified air (relative humidity, humidifier temperature and pressure). Inlet, Outlet, No Flux, Water Condensation-Evaporation and Water Gas Shift subnodes attach here.
tools.usage: Hydrogen Fuel Cell > H2 Gas Phase (h2gasph1) / O2 Gas Phase (o2gasph1); Java types: "H2GasPhase", "O2GasPhase"

parameters.name: RH_hum, T_hum, pA_hum
parameters.description: Humidifier relative humidity, temperature and absolute pressure.

parameters.name: Gas diffusivities
parameters.description: Binary Maxwell-Stefan diffusivities (built in or user defined).

tools.notes: Humidified air uses dry mole fractions 0.79 N2, 4e-4 CO2 and 1e-6 CO internally.

tools.name: Membrane (fc/we)
tools.description: Domain node where only the Electrolyte Phase is active, representing an ion-exchange membrane or solid electrolyte. It defines gas crossover (permeation coefficients and Henry's law constants for H2, O2, N2, including heat of parasitic crossover reactions) and, when enabled, electroosmotic water drag with vapor- or liquid-equilibrated water transport, water activity and heat of absorption.
tools.usage: Hydrogen Fuel Cell / Water Electrolyzer > Membrane (mem1); Java: model.component("comp1").physics("fc").create("mem1", "Membrane", 3)

parameters.name: Psi_H2, Psi_O2, Psi_N2 / H_H2...
parameters.description: Permeation and Henry's law coefficients for crossover.

parameters.name: xi, alpha
parameters.description: Electroosmotic drag coefficient and water transport coefficient.

parameters.name: aw_mem
parameters.description: Water activity (e.g. RH) when drag is not solved.

tools.notes: Water Absorption-Desorption boundary nodes are added automatically at membrane-gas phase interfaces when electroosmotic drag is on.

tools.name: Current Collector / Separator (fc/we)
tools.description: Layer nodes of the fuel cell and electrolyzer interfaces. Current Collector activates only the Electronic Conducting Phase with an electric conductivity (bipolar plates, ribs, current collectors, optionally with cooling). Separator activates only the Electrolyte Phase in a porous matrix, typically the diaphragm between two gas-electrolyte compartments of a liquid-electrolyte electrolyzer, with Bruggeman, tortuosity or user-defined conductivity correction.
tools.usage: Hydrogen Fuel Cell / Water Electrolyzer > Current Collector (cc1) / Separator (sep1); Java: model.component("comp1").physics("fc").create("cc1", "CurrentCollector", 3)

parameters.name: sigmas_mat / sigma
parameters.description: Electric conductivity of the current collector.

parameters.name: epsl, IonicCorrModel
parameters.description: Separator electrolyte volume fraction and correction model.

tools.notes: Current Collector domains are also where Electric Ground and Electric Potential subnodes are usually applied.

tools.name: H2/O2 Gas Diffusion Layer (fc/we)
tools.description: Domain node where the Electronic Conducting Phase and the gas phase of one side are active, representing gas diffusion layers or porous transport layers. It sets the effective electric conductivity, gas pore volume fraction with diffusivity correction (Bruggeman, tortuosity, user defined), gas permeability for Darcy flow, and optional pore-wall (Knudsen) interaction.
tools.usage: Hydrogen Fuel Cell > H2 Gas Diffusion Layer (h2gdl1) / O2 Gas Diffusion Layer (o2gdl1); Java: model.component("comp1").physics("fc").create("h2gdl1", "H2GasDiffusionLayer", 3)

parameters.name: epsg, DiffusionCorrModel
parameters.description: Gas pore volume fraction and correction.

parameters.name: IncludePoreWallInteractions, d_pore
parameters.description: Knudsen wall diffusivity with pore diameter.

tools.notes: Microporous layers can be modelled as additional GDL domains with different properties.

tools.name: H2/O2 Gas Diffusion Electrode and Gas Diffusion Electrode Reaction (fc/we)
tools.description: Three-phase domain node (electronic, electrolyte and gas phases active) for catalyst layers, with effective electronic and ionic conductivities, gas transport corrections and permeability. Its H2/O2 Gas Diffusion Electrode Reaction subnodes define stoichiometry, equilibrium potential (built-in from thermodynamics, Nernst, material or user), reference partial pressures, exchange current density and transfer coefficients, and the active specific surface area Av. A Porous Matrix Double-Layer Capacitance subnode enables impedance simulations.
tools.usage: Hydrogen Fuel Cell > H2/O2 Gas Diffusion Electrode (h2gde1, o2gde1) > Gas Diffusion Electrode Reaction (h2gder1, o2gder1); Java: model.component("comp1").physics("fc").create("o2gde1", "O2GasDiffusionElectrode", 3)

parameters.name: i0_ref
parameters.description: Reference exchange current density at the reference partial pressures.

parameters.name: Eeq_mat / Eeq
parameters.description: Equilibrium potential source (built in by default).

parameters.name: IonicCorrModel, epsl, epsg
parameters.description: Electrolyte and gas volume fractions and corrections.

tools.notes: Mass sources from the reactions are applied automatically to the gas phase; with a separate flow interface use Reacting Flow, H2/O2 Gas Phase to pass them on.

tools.name: Thin H2/O2 Gas Diffusion Electrode (fc/we)
tools.description: Boundary version of the gas diffusion electrode for catalyst layers thin enough that gradients through the thickness can be neglected, placed between electrolyte, electronic and gas phases. Volumetric reaction currents of its Thin Gas Diffusion Electrode Reaction subnodes are multiplied by the electrode thickness and applied as boundary sources; film (contact) resistance can be included. It avoids meshing thin catalyst layers in 3D cell models.
tools.usage: Hydrogen Fuel Cell > Thin H2 Gas Diffusion Electrode (th2gde1) / Thin O2 Gas Diffusion Electrode (to2gde1) > Thin ... Reaction (th2gder1, to2gder1); Java: model.component("comp1").physics("fc").create("to2gde1", "ThinO2GasDiffusionElectrode", 2)

parameters.name: Av, i0_ref, alphaa
parameters.description: Reaction parameters in the reaction subnodes.

tools.notes: Use porous GDE domains when oxygen transport limitations inside the catalyst layer matter.

tools.name: H2/O2 Gas-Electrolyte Compartment (Water Electrolyzer)
tools.description: Domain node where the electrolyte phase and one gas phase are both active, representing a hydrogen- or oxygen-evolving electrolyte compartment of a liquid-electrolyte electrolyzer. Gas holdup reduces the electrolyte volume fraction and effective conductivity (Bruggeman, tortuosity, user), and gas transport corrections, permeability and Knudsen pore-wall interactions can be set.
tools.usage: Water Electrolyzer > H2 Gas-Electrolyte Compartment (h2gec1) / O2 Gas-Electrolyte Compartment (o2gec1); Java: model.component("comp1").physics("we").create("h2gec1", "H2GasElectrolyteCompartment", 2)

parameters.name: epsl, IonicCorrModel
parameters.description: Electrolyte volume fraction (from gas fraction) and correction.

parameters.name: epsg, DiffusionCorrModel
parameters.description: Gas volume fraction and gas diffusion correction.

tools.notes: The gas volume fraction can come from a coupled bubbly-flow or Euler-Euler model.

tools.name: H2/O2 Electrode Surface (Water Electrolyzer)
tools.description: Boundary nodes defining planar electrode surfaces on exterior boundaries of H2 or O2 Gas-Electrolyte Compartments, with an electric potential or current condition and Electrode Reaction subnodes (hydrogen or oxygen evolution). Film resistance can represent contact resistance or deposits. Internal H2/O2 Electrode Surface variants are used for interior electrodes, for example in stacks with shunt currents.
tools.usage: Water Electrolyzer > H2 Electrode Surface (h2es1) / O2 Electrode Surface (o2es1) > H2/O2 Electrode Reaction; Java: model.component("comp1").physics("we").create("h2es1", "H2ElectrodeSurface", 1)

parameters.name: Electrode phase potential condition
parameters.description: Electric potential, electrode potential, total current, average current density.

parameters.name: H2/O2 Electrode Reaction
parameters.description: Kinetics and equilibrium potential of HER/OER.

parameters.name: Film Resistance
parameters.description: Surface resistance or thickness and conductivity.

tools.notes: Java types for the internal variants are InternalH2ElectrodeSurface and InternalO2ElectrodeSurface.

tools.name: H2/O2 Gas Flow Channel (fc/we)
tools.description: Domain node where only one gas phase is active, representing gas channels. With gas-phase diffusion the diffusivities come from the Gas Phase node; with Darcy's law the permeability can be set for straight channels using the analytical Boussinesq expression for rectangular cross sections, giving correct average flow without solving Navier-Stokes. Streamline diffusion stabilization is applied in channels by default.
tools.usage: Hydrogen Fuel Cell > H2 Gas Flow Channel (h2fch1) / O2 Gas Flow Channel (o2fch1); Java: model.component("comp1").physics("fc").create("o2fch1", "O2FlowChannel", 3)

parameters.name: Gas permeability
parameters.description: Straight channels (height, width) or user defined.

tools.notes: For curved channels or local velocity profiles couple Laminar Flow with Reacting Flow, H2/O2 Gas Phase.

tools.name: H2/O2 Inlet and Outlet (fc/we)
tools.description: Boundary conditions on exterior gas-phase boundaries. H2/O2 Inlet sets the inflow composition by a mixture composition constraint (mole fractions, humidified mixture or air) or by mass flow rates, including a Stoichiometric feed option where flow follows from a stoichiometric current and stoichiometric number; with Darcy's law the inlet pressure or flow is also set. H2/O2 Outlet lets gas leave by convection and sets the outlet pressure for Darcy flow.
tools.usage: H2/O2 Gas Phase > H2 Inlet (h2in1) / O2 Inlet (o2in1) / H2 Outlet / O2 Outlet; Java: model.component("comp1").physics("fc").feature("o2gasph1").create("o2in1", "O2Inlet", 2)

parameters.name: ifStoichiometricFeed, stoich_I, stoich_numO2
parameters.description: Stoichiometric feed with current and stoichiometric number.

tools.notes: Stoichiometric feed is the default for fuel-cell operation mode.

tools.name: Water Condensation-Evaporation (fc/we)
tools.description: Gas Phase subnode adding a mass source for water condensation or evaporation when the vapor partial pressure exceeds or falls below the saturation pressure, typical of low-temperature fuel cells and electrolyzers. The rate is computed from the vapor pressure with a rate constant or given by a user expression, and the heat of reaction is built in.
tools.usage: H2/O2 Gas Phase > Water Condensation-Evaporation (wce1); Java: model.component("comp1").physics("fc").feature("o2gasph1").create("wce1", "WaterCondensationEvaporation", 3)
tools.notes: Requires H2O in the gas mixture and gas-phase diffusion or Darcy's law.

tools.name: Water Gas Shift Reaction (fc/we)
tools.description: H2 Gas Phase subnode adding the CO + H2O <=> CO2 + H2 reaction as a mass source, relevant for reformate-fed and molten carbonate fuel cells and for solid oxide co-electrolysis. The rate follows the mass action law with a rate constant and reference pressure or a user expression; the heat of reaction is built in or user defined.
tools.usage: H2 Gas Phase > Water Gas Shift Reaction (wgsr1); Java type: "WaterGasShiftReaction"
tools.notes: Requires H2O, CO and CO2 selected in the H2 gas mixture with gas-phase diffusion.

tools.name: Water Absorption-Desorption (Membrane, fc/we)
tools.description: Boundary nodes added by default at membrane-gas phase interfaces (H2 side and O2 side) when electroosmotic water drag is enabled. They set the water flux between membrane and gas phase through vapor absorption-desorption kinetics, liquid water pressure, water chemical potential, or a user rate, and contribute a heat source from the heat of absorption. Water Flux and Water Chemical Potential are advanced membrane boundary conditions.
tools.usage: Hydrogen Fuel Cell > Water Absorption-Desorption, H2 Side (wadh2side1) / O2 Side (wado2side1); Java types: "WaterAbsorptionDesorptionH2Side", "WaterAbsorptionDesorptionO2Side"

parameters.name: Absorption-desorption condition
parameters.description: From parent, vapor absorption-desorption, liquid water pressure, chemical potential or user-defined rate.

tools.example: Application Library: Fuel_Cell_and_Electrolyzer_Module/Fuel_Cells/pem_mea_1d (membrane hydration and water balance).
tools.notes: Selections are locked to membrane-gas phase intersection boundaries.

tools.name: Internal Electrode / Electrolyte Contact Resistance (fc/we)
tools.description: Subnodes of the Electronic Conducting Phase or Electrolyte Phase that add a contact resistance on interior boundaries, implemented as slit boundaries with separate potential degrees of freedom on each side and a resistive current condition between them. Used for GDL-bipolar plate contact resistance or membrane-electrode interface resistance.
tools.usage: Electronic Conducting Phase > Internal Electrode Contact Resistance (ieccr1); Electrolyte Phase > Internal Electrolyte Contact Resistance; Java: model.component("comp1").physics("fc").feature("ecph1").create("ieccr1", "InternalElectrodeContactResistance", 2)
tools.notes: Contact resistance also generates Joule heat included in Electrochemical Heating.

tools.name: Built-in Equilibrium and Thermoneutral Potentials (fc/we)
tools.description: Theory for the Built in reference equilibrium potential of fuel-cell and electrolyzer electrode reactions: reaction enthalpy and entropy from temperature-dependent species data at 1 atm give Gibbs energy, equilibrium potential and thermoneutral voltage, expressed versus a reversible hydrogen electrode of the same electrolyte at a specified reference temperature. HOR/HER are therefore near 0 V and ORR/OER near the cell equilibrium voltage.
tools.usage: Gas Diffusion Electrode Reaction > Equilibrium Potential > Reference equilibrium potential = Built in

parameters.name: Hion, Sion
parameters.description: Enthalpy and entropy of the charge-carrying ion (affect thermoneutral voltage).

tools.example: Evaluate fc.o2gde1.o2gder1.Eeq and the thermoneutral voltage in a Global Evaluation to check the reversible heat of a PEM cell at 80 degC.
tools.notes: Only the gas species have built-in thermodynamic data; ion properties are user settings.

tools.name: Reacting Flow, H2/O2 Gas Phase (multiphysics coupling)
tools.description: Couplings that link a fluid flow interface (Laminar Flow, Brinkman, Free and Porous Media Flow) to the H2 or O2 gas phase of a Hydrogen Fuel Cell or Water Electrolyzer interface. The flow interface supplies velocity and pressure to the fc/we gas transport, while fc/we supplies mixture density and viscosity back, giving two-way coupled gas flow and species transport in channels and porous layers.
tools.usage: Multiphysics > Reacting Flow, H2 Gas Phase (rfh1) / Reacting Flow, O2 Gas Phase (rfo1); Java: model.component("comp1").multiphysics().create("rfh1", "ReactingFlowH2GasPhase", 3)

parameters.name: fc/we interface
parameters.description: Source of density, viscosity and mass sources.

tools.notes: When these couplings are used, disable the built-in Darcy option in the corresponding gas mixture.

tools.name: Aqueous Electrolyte Transport (aqt)
tools.description: Interface for Nernst-Planck transport of any number of species in water-based electrolytes with electroneutrality and built-in water auto-ionization, where species can be strong and weak acids and bases, ampholytes, carbonic acid, complexes and uncharged species with their equilibria handled automatically. It suits corrosion chemistry, atmospheric corrosion films and pH-dependent electrochemistry; electrode surfaces and porous electrodes can be included.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Electrochemistry > Aqueous Electrolyte Transport (aqt); Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("aqt", "AqueousElectrolyteTransport", "geom1")

parameters.name: prop("TransportMechanism") Convection / SolveElectrolytePhasePotential
parameters.description: Convection and whether to solve for the electrolyte potential.

parameters.name: Electrolyte > species subnodes
parameters.description: Fully Dissociated, Weak Acid, Weak Base, Ampholyte, Carbonic Acid, Complex, Uncharged.

tools.notes: Dependent variables are the electrolyte potential and the concentrations of species added by each species node.

tools.name: Species Nodes: Fully Dissociated / Weak Acid / Weak Base / Ampholyte / Uncharged (Aqueous Electrolyte Transport)
tools.description: Subnodes of the aqt Electrolyte node that each add a species with its equilibrium chemistry: Fully Dissociated Species (strong acids/bases and salts, with charge number), Weak Acid and Weak Base (monoprotic or polyprotic with pKa values), Ampholyte (charge from equilibrium constants with base charge z0 or an average-charge function of pH) and Uncharged Species. Diffusivities and mobilities are set per species.
tools.usage: Aqueous Electrolyte Transport > Electrolyte (el1) > Fully Dissociated Species (fds1) / Weak Acid (wa1) / Weak Base / Ampholyte (amph1) / Uncharged Species (uns1); Java types: "FullyDissociatedSpecies", "WeakAcid", "WeakBase", "Ampholyte", "UnchargedSpecies"

parameters.name: Immobile species
parameters.description: Option to fix a species in place.

tools.notes: Do not add H+ or OH- explicitly; water auto-ionization is built into the interface.

tools.name: Carbonic Acid / Complex Species (Aqueous Electrolyte Transport)
tools.description: Specialized species nodes of Aqueous Electrolyte Transport. Carbonic Acid adds all dissolved carbon dioxide species (CO2(aq), H2CO3, HCO3-, CO3 2-) with built-in temperature-dependent pKa values or user values. Complex Species defines a complex formed from available species with a formation equilibrium constant Keq, diffusion coefficient and stoichiometric coefficients (negative or zero).
tools.usage: Aqueous Electrolyte Transport > Electrolyte > Carbonic Acid (carb1) / Complex Species (coms1); Java types: "CarbonicAcid", "ComplexSpecies"

parameters.name: pKa (Carbonic Acid)
parameters.description: Built in (temperature dependent) or user defined.

tools.notes: Complex Species is available once at least one mobile species exists.

tools.name: Reservoir (Aqueous Electrolyte Transport)
tools.description: Boundary condition for a boundary facing a well-mixed electrolyte reservoir, constraining the species concentrations (for weak acids, bases and ampholytes only the total of all dissociation forms) and setting the electrolyte potential by insulation or a fixed value. Complex species are subtracted automatically from the complex-forming species.
tools.usage: Aqueous Electrolyte Transport > Reservoir (rev1); Java: model.component("comp1").physics("aqt").create("rev1", "Reservoir", 0)
tools.notes: Uses pointwise constraints on the concentration variables.

tools.name: Concentrated Electrolyte Transport (cet)
tools.description: Interface for electrolytes with large concentration gradients of the charge-carrying ions, where no neutral solvent or supporting electrolyte can be assumed (molten salts, concentrated KOH, battery electrolytes). Species transport follows the Onsager-Stefan-Maxwell equations with binary interactions between all species; with electroneutrality, n species reduce to n-2 electrolyte-component unknowns plus the electrolyte potential, which is defined relative to a reference electrode reaction.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Electrochemistry > Concentrated Electrolyte Transport (cet); Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("cet", "ConcentratedElectrolyteTransport", "geom1")

parameters.name: prop("Species") CationNames, CationCharges, CationMasses (and anions, neutrals)
parameters.description: Species definition; at least one cation and one anion.

parameters.name: Electrolyte > Diffusion Coefficients
parameters.description: Maxwell-Stefan diffusivities of all binary pairs.

parameters.name: Reference Electrode
parameters.description: Reference reaction stoichiometry defining the electrolyte potential.

tools.notes: Electrolyte component names are generated from the species (e.g. Fe_OH_2, H2O).

tools.name: Diffusion Coefficients / Reference Electrode (Concentrated Electrolyte Transport)
tools.description: Subnodes of the cet Electrolyte node. Diffusion Coefficients defines Maxwell-Stefan diffusivities that relate chemical potential gradients to flux differences for all binary species pairs. Reference Electrode defines the reduction-reaction stoichiometry of a reference electrode, so the electrolyte potential equals an experimentally measurable voltage; it is also used for a reference-electrode-based mass-averaged velocity and for fluxes under an Electrolyte Potential condition.
tools.usage: Concentrated Electrolyte Transport > Electrolyte > Diffusion Coefficients (dc1); Reference Electrode (ref1); Java types: "DiffusionCoefficients", "ReferenceElectrode"

parameters.name: Reference stoichiometry
parameters.description: Nonzero for at least one cation or anion; electron on the left side.

tools.notes: Separator and Species Sources nodes complete porous and reacting cet models.

tools.name: Electrode, Shell (els)
tools.description: Boundary-level interface for tangential current conduction in thin electrodes (seed layers, foils, thin films) where the potential variation through the thickness is negligible, replacing the thin domain by a PDE on the boundary with Ohm's law. The Electrode node sets the shell thickness and conductivity; it couples to a current distribution interface through electrode potentials and currents. The Electrodeposition and Corrosion Modules add Depositing Electrode and Corroding Electrode nodes that update the thickness.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Electrochemistry > Electrode, Shell (els); Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("els", "ElectrodeShell", "geom1")

parameters.name: Ground / Electric Potential / Normal Current Density / Boundary Current Source

tools.notes: The Electrode node (ece1) takes the conductivity from the material by default; Depositing Electrode (Electrodeposition Module) and Corroding Electrode (Corrosion Module) let the shell thickness evolve with the deposition/dissolution rate.

tools.name: Electroanalysis (tcd)
tools.description: Model Wizard entry adding a Tertiary Current Distribution, Nernst-Planck interface with the Electroanalysis charge conservation model: the electrolyte contains excess supporting electrolyte, ohmic losses are neglected (electrolyte potential set to zero), and only the electroactive species concentrations are solved by diffusion and optional convection. Electrode surfaces use concentration-dependent (electroanalytical Butler-Volmer) kinetics; typical uses are cyclic voltammetry, chronoamperometry, sensors and EIS.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Electrochemistry > Electroanalysis (tcd); Java: model.component("comp1").physics().create("tcd", "TertiaryElectroanalysis", "geom1")

parameters.name: Electrode Surface boundary condition
parameters.description: Electrode potential, cyclic voltammetry, counter electrode, harmonic perturbation.

tools.notes: The Java type is TertiaryElectroanalysis although the default name is tcd.

tools.name: Cyclic Voltammetry (Electrode Surface condition and study step)
tools.description: Built-in cyclic voltammetry setup: the Electrode Surface boundary condition Cyclic voltammetry sweeps the electrode potential linearly between vertex potentials at a given scan rate for a number of cycles (with optional start/end potentials, smoothing and solver events at vertices), and the Cyclic Voltammetry study step sets up a time-dependent solver whose duration and step size follow these settings, adding a stop condition at the end of cycling. The resulting voltammogram plots current versus potential.
tools.usage: Electrode Surface > Boundary condition = Cyclic voltammetry; Study > Cyclic Voltammetry (cyclv); Java: model.component("comp1").physics("tcd").feature("es1").set("BoundaryCondition", "CyclicVoltammetry"); model.study("std1").create("cyclv", "CyclicVoltammetry")

parameters.name: EnableTimeSmoothing, smoothingfactor, EnableVertexPotentialsEvents
parameters.description: Smoothing and solver events at vertices.

tools.notes: Available with the Battery Design, Corrosion, Electrochemistry, Electrodeposition and Fuel Cell & Electrolyzer Modules. Without an active cyclic-voltammetry Electrode Surface no stop condition is added; a plain Time Dependent study also works.

tools.name: Electroanalytical Butler-Volmer Equation and Counter Electrode (Electroanalysis)
tools.description: Theory used by the Electroanalysis model: electrode kinetics written with a heterogeneous rate constant k0 and cathodic transfer coefficient (alphaa + alphac = 1 for one electron), reducing to the Nernst equation at zero current and to the classical Butler-Volmer form with i0 = k0*F*c. Because the electrolyte potential is not solved, an overall charge balance is imposed by the Counter electrode boundary condition, which adds one counter-electrode potential unknown so that all electrode currents sum to zero.
tools.usage: Electroanalysis > Electrode Surface > Electrode Reaction (Butler-Volmer with i0Type = MassActionLaw and rate constant k), Electrode Surface boundary condition = Counter electrode

parameters.name: CounterElectrode
parameters.description: Boundary condition value for charge balance.

tools.notes: Only one counter-electrode potential is added regardless of the number of counter electrodes.
